summary: This reference maps Bunzai's canonical conversion engine, scene runtime and host layers. Every external format maps through one canonical superset; escrow retains original source and binary carriers without carrying private or executable payloads across formats. KindAdapter contracts, exhaustive shape parity and strict canonical decoders reject schema drift, while serialization reports describe loss. Detection ranks kind-correct adapters and folder discovery supplies the registry. Bundles extract and re-embed lorebooks. Semantic capabilities cover pure previews, progressive discovery, bounded reads, persistent drafts, result eviction and paging, independently approved documentation, and explicit durable apply with revision checks and re-read verification. Layering reuses the same engine across the CLI, installed Studio and static browser Studio. The encrypted stage separates versioned pieces, Studio documents and chats; folders remain import/export boundaries. Its source map names database, crypto, snapshot, health, asset and search owners. Scale and release claims require bounded, artifact-matched evidence. The reusable roleplay source API keeps the current canonical turn orchestration and injects stores, providers and readers. Its runtime owns live turns, gates, tracker rounds, recovery and accepted host task completion through shutdown. Desktop consumes it; a caller-owned terminal runner is unit-proven. Browser bundling and a scripted Node turn establish source compatibility only. A standalone shared-library terminal command awaits durable cross-process checkpoint ownership; packaged release behavior remains separately unverified.

sections.title: The one idea: hub and spoke
sections.summary: Every external format maps to and from one canonical superset rather than converting directly to every other format. A pairwise mesh requires N times N minus one paths; hub and spoke needs only N adapters. Adding a format therefore adds one adapter without changing existing formats or core conversion logic. Import calls the adapter's toCanonical operation, export calls fromCanonical, and conversion composes those two steps. This is the architectural invariant behind adapter independence and honest interoperability.

sections.title: The canonical entity
sections.summary: src/core/canonical.ts defines the shared wrapper: schemaVersion identifies the canonical revision, kind selects the entity family, id is the stable identity, body contains interoperable content, profiles hold sparse per-platform overrides, and original holds source escrow. Character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, and quickreply are adapter-backed kinds; canonical schemas also define pack and htmldoc entities. Body details live in their entity folders rather than in the wrapper. The superset rule limits body fields to meaning represented by at least one real wire format. Values that exist only in one application's memory or have no portable producer remain in escrow instead of acquiring a misleading canonical slot.

children.title: The superset rule
children.summary: Canonical bodies contain only fields serialized by real formats. A field earns a first-class slot only when a wire producer exists. Application-only values, including five RoleCall lorebook fields, stay escrowed so Bunzai does not promise unsupported portability.

sections.title: Escrow: semantic round-trips, contained cross-format loss
sections.summary: Escrow preserves parsed source snapshots and unmapped fields for semantic same-format round trips. Byte identity is limited to explicitly specified fixture-proven tiers. Entity parts isolate escrow from light editor reads; light media stays sealed with stable references, while legacy blobbed authored text is materialized only when needed. Conversion follows hub and spoke with explicit loss reporting.

sections.title: The adapter contract
sections.summary: The adapter contract: src/core/adapter.ts defines one generic KindAdapter<K> (kind, toCanonical returning that kind's canonical piece, fromCanonical with an optional EmitContext that carries embedded lorebooks) and FormatAdapter as the union of it over every kind in the generated kind seam; character cards add extractLorebook and presets add extractRegex and embedRegex. Formats are open drop-in folders; kinds are a closed set that grows by adding an entities/<kind>/ folder with its kind.ts and running bun run kinds. Adapter output carries text or bytes, suggestedExtension, and a SerializeReport naming escrowed, dropped, shadowed, and warning paths; escrowFormatIds declares family-keyed twins such as rolecall-preset owning original.rolecall, so loss reporting excludes genuine same-format escrow. Canonical JSON crosses storage and HTTP through src/entities/runtime-schema.ts, which unions every kind's whole-entity entitySchema (the shared envelope in _shared/envelope.ts plus its body) collected by the generated kind seam. Each runtime schema uses defineExhaustiveShape<T>() for exact input and output parity; missing or extra keys, narrowed unions, coercion, any, and never fail typecheck. Storage, HTTP save, format-corpus verification, and Kit drafts share this ADR-011 boundary.

sections.title: Detection and the registry
sections.summary: src/core/registry.ts holds the in-memory adapter table. Detection runs every adapter, rejects scores at or below 0.5, and selects the single highest-confidence match. Scores encode specificity: a RoleCall card can score 1.0 and outrank the generic SillyTavern reader at 0.9 for the same compatible CCv3 payload. Because character and lorebook adapters share one registry, detectors also enforce a cross-kind firewall. A bare name is insufficient evidence for SillyTavern flat-v1 character data; at least one genuine character signal such as description, personality, scenario, first_mes, or mes_example is required, preventing a name-bearing worldbook from being misclassified.

sections.title: Folders-as-schema (the moddability promise)
sections.summary: src/core/loader.ts is the impure discovery edge. It scans src/formats/*/index.ts with filesystem primitives, dynamically imports each module, and registers its default export. Names beginning with an underscore, including _shared and _template, are ignored. A folder may export one adapter or an array when a format family supplies multiple codecs. Agnai, Risu, SillyTavern, and RoleCall each include character and lorebook codecs; some arrays also include regex, persona, preset, or quick-reply codecs. FormatId is an open string rather than a central enum. Adding a format means copying the template, implementing detection and both canonical directions, and supplying proof; no core registry list or unrelated format file is edited.

sections.title: Bundles: a card plus its lorebook
sections.summary: CCv2 and CCv3 character cards can embed a character_book, but Bunzai models that book as a separate canonical lorebook referenced by the character rather than leaving an opaque nested blob. During import, shared bundle logic extracts the book, creates a CanonicalLorebook, and records its id in knowledgeRefs. During export, the character adapter receives resolved lorebooks through EmitContext and embeds the appropriate target-format representation. The resolved list is authoritative even when empty: removing a link or disabling all linked books clears stale embedded data from the escrowed source twin. convertFile coordinates extraction and re-embedding for ordinary same-kind conversions, keeping bundle behavior format-agnostic at the canonical layer.

sections.title: Semantic content capabilities
sections.summary: Capability folders provide pure operations returning previews, changes, warnings, and platform impact without writing. Kit projects content, studio, transfer, and diagnostics into one catalog. Only pure content gets exact read-or-draft access; deferred apply and writable bridges fail closed until separate safety policy grants an exact name. Search exposes five matches, browse and describe progressively, hidden or duplicate descriptors fail, and deferred exposure resets each user turn while drafts persist. studio_read uses RFC 6901 pointers and paging; oversized values use result_query handles whose store enforces per-entry and aggregate UTF-8 byte caps, a count cap, oldest-first eviction, character paging, and direct-offset recovery beyond capacity. change_query retains proposals; read-effect tools return deterministic observations and are rejected for changing content or claiming changes. docs_query searches indexed metadata and reads authoritative Markdown without arbitrary paths or network. Summaries enter generated indexes only with independent hash-bound APPROVE receipts; source or summary edits invalidate approval. Focused checks validate an author's sidecar; global checks require every approval and current projections. Security classifies only exact catalog-derived names as preview-only; durable apply remains an explicit compareAndSave write with re-read verification.

sections.title: Layering
sections.summary: Core owns pure canonical computation and shared synchronous derivation; entity schemas and capabilities own semantic shape; codecs convert through canonical; Stage storage backends remain opaque. Light editor reads, selected escrow and native asset metadata feed conditional patch saves without full escrow/media opens. D18 prevents backend imports of engine, entity or format code.

sections.title: The stage (chat runtime, in progress)
sections.summary: Stage stores encrypted pieces and chats behind contracts; scene turns assemble prompts through Kit providers. A SillyTavern chat imports in one transaction (rule 29); a message can be hidden (rule 30); a turn writes a reply, a version, or a continuation (rule 31); a cut message is purged after 1 day, other trash after 3 (rule 11). Guides and saved scene setups are StateStore documents the folder export carries. Runtime, migrations and packaged proof remain unrun.

sections.title: Reusable roleplay core
sections.summary: createRoleplayCore exposes canonical turns and the Dramaturg with injected stores, providers and readers. One runtime owns controllers, gates, tracker rounds, recovery and accepted host tasks; shutdown cancels and awaits owned writes. ChatStore owns the sealed, revision-guarded Dramaturg conversation in migration 46, preserved by snapshots alongside existing scene state. Desktop supplies library hooks; a terminal runner accepts a configured core. Browser and Node checks prove source compatibility, not published or packaged behavior.

sections.title: The CLI
sections.summary: The thin CLI provides conversion, inspection, labeling, validation, formats, Studio launch, folder export, derived-cache commands, version and help. A separate injected terminal session runner handles text, continue, swipe and quit using the same core and scene writes. It fails applicable imported regex closed without a worker. Scripted tests cover the runner; a standalone shared-library command is withheld until durable cross-process checkpoint ownership makes recovery safe.

sections.title: Source of truth
sections.summary: The map names canonical, registry, adapter, loader, format overlay, MIME, bundles, derivation, database, encryption and entity owners, now including snapshots, the health check and the host-only care routes. Scale evidence is bounded and artifact-matched; CLI launch differs from desktop identity; source paths are reviewed while runtime metrics and physical RSS remain unproved.
